No obstruction'. Note 3 (timing of installation) matches. Note 4 (pervious paving) matches. Note 5 is completely incorrect: states 'COMBUSTIBLE CONSTRUCTION NON-CONFORMANCE' instead of required text about 'Commercial dumpsters and containers with an individual capacity of 1.5 cubic yards or greater'. Note 6 (fire lanes) matches. Note 7 (vertical clearance) matches.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires ~90% semantic matching for the 7 standard Austin Fire notes. Of the 7 notes, only 5 have semantically correct content (notes 1, 3, 4, 6, 7). Note 2 contains garbled/incorrect wording that changes the meaning, and note 5 discusses an entirely different topic ('combustible construction non-conformance' instead of dumpster placement near combustible elements). This yields approximately 71% match (5 of 7 notes), which falls below the 90% threshold required by the validation methodology.
findings.explanation: Fire Department notes on Sheet 5 have only 71% semantic match (5 of 7 notes correct); note 2 has garbled text and note 5 discusses wrong topic (combustible construction instead of dumpsters).
findings.resolution: Correct Fire Department note 2 to state: 'Hydrants must be installed with the center of the four-inch opening at least 18 inches above finished grade. The four-inch opening must face the driveway or street with three- to six-foot setbacks from the curbline(s). No obstruction is allowed within three feet of any hydrant and the four-inch opening must be totally unobstructed from the street.' Correct Fire Department note 5 to state: 'Commercial dumpsters and containers with an individual capacity of 1.5 cubic yards or greater shall not be stored or placed within ten feet of openings, combustible walls, or combustible eave lines.' See the CoA standard notes template at https://austin.widen.net/s/vxznrtmfwf/sp_consolidatedsiteplanapplication_notestemplates for the expected notes.

summary: 9 of 11 items pass, 1 fails, 2 not-applicable. Fire Department standard notes (AF-01) fail due to incorrect wording in notes 2 and 5.
